title: Strong Converse Exponent of Quantum State Merging
authors: Mario Berta, Hao-Chung Cheng, Roberto Rubboli, Marco Tomamichel
abstract: We determine the strong converse exponent for the entanglement cost of quantum state merging, showing that it is characterized by the optimized $α$-$z$ conditional Rényi entropies with $z=α/2\in[1/2,1]$. This contrasts with the sandwiched conditional Rényi entropies that typically govern strong converse exponents in quantum information theory. As a consequence, we derive the strong converse exponent of the partially smoothed conditional min-entropy in purified distance. This exponent is governed by club-sandwiched conditional entropies, whereas global smoothing leads to a sandwiched expression.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the exact strong converse exponent for quantum state merging, a key task in quantum information theory. It establishes that this exponent is governed by optimized $\alpha$-$z$ conditional Rényi entropies, which differs from standard results. The findings provide rigorous bounds on the achievable rates for quantum information transfer protocols.
main_problem: The paper determines the strong converse exponent for the entanglement cost associated with quantum state merging.
main_result: The strong converse exponent is characterized by optimized $\alpha$-$z$ conditional Rényi entropies, contrasting with typical results governed by sandwiched conditional Rényi entropies.
method: The analysis adapts the club-sandwiched converse method and utilizes techniques from Schatten-norm Hölder theory to establish asymptotic bounds on the fidelity decay.
model_or_system: The study concerns the quantum state merging task, where a tripartite pure state $\psi_{ABR}$ is used to transfer information from Alice (A) to Bob, preserving coherence relative to an inaccessible reference system R.
key_observables: Entanglement Cost ($r$), Squared Fidelity ($F$), Purified Distance, and various conditional Rényi entropies ($H^{\uparrow}_{\alpha, \alpha/2}(A|B)_{\psi}$).
important_parameters: The exponent depends on the optimization parameter $\alpha \in [1/2, 1]$ and the rate $r$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and focuses on the strong converse regime where the optimal fidelity decays exponentially.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the quantum state merging protocol. Table I summarizes the strong converse and error exponents for different smoothing types (Globally vs. Partially smoothed).
paper_structure: The paper develops the result by establishing upper and lower bounds on the fidelity decay rate, comparing the constraints imposed by global vs. partial smoothing, and deriving the final exponent using variational representations.
why_interesting: The precise characterization of the strong converse exponent using specific conditional entropy forms provides deep insights into the fundamental limits of quantum information processing tasks.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Illustration of the quantum state merging task protocol. Left: Alice and Bob share n copies of a tripartite pure state |ψ⟩⊗n ABR alongside preshared entanglement of Schmidt rank |Kn|. Right: After applying a one-way local operation and classical communication (LOCC) protocol, Alice’s system An is merged at Bob’s side, consuming or distilling entanglement such that the final entangled state has a Schmidt rank of |Ln|.
